stem: First-stage vector search is approximate because…
options: Query and chunk are embedded separately — the model never sees them together
explanation: Which is why it is fast, and why a reranker can do better on a short list.

options: Reads query and candidate together and orders a few dozen precisely — too expensive for the corpus, fine for twenty
explanation: Two stages: cheap recall, expensive precision.

options: Chatty, multi-part or pronoun-laden messages, and vocabulary mismatch between users and documents
explanation: Turn a message into a search query before retrieval.

options: Asking the model for a hypothetical answer and searching with that, because answers look like documents

stem: The LLM reranker in the example versus a cross-encoder…
options: Zero setup but slower and costlier; a cross-encoder is the production version of the same job

stem: Reranking 200 candidates at 400 ms is slow. The fix…
options: Rerank fewer candidates (20–30) and verify hit@k holds
explanation: The expensive step is meant to run over a handful.

stem: Keep a rewrite or rerank step when…
options: It moves hit@k on the golden set — otherwise it is latency and cost for nothing
The corpus is tiny and clean
The corpus is large or noisy and the right passage is in the top-20 but not the top-3
explanation: hit@20 high, hit@3 low is the signal.

stem: A message asks two questions. The rewriter should…
options: Produce two queries, retrieve for both, and merge (e.g. with RRF) or label per sub-question

stem: Parent–child retrieval returns to the model…
options: The enclosing section of the small chunks that matched, de-duplicated by parent
explanation: Precise retrieval, enough context to answer.
